message.content:
**Yes – you can report a noise complaint in Atlanta.**  
In the United States, noise enforcement is typically handled by the city’s police department or the city’s 311 service, rather than by the city council itself. Here’s how you can do it:

| Step | What to Do | Where to Go / Who to Call |
|------|------------|---------------------------|
| 1 | **Identify the source and time** of the noise (e.g., loud music, construction, barking dogs). | — |
| 2 | **Call the Atlanta Police Department (APD)** for immediate or urgent complaints. | **APD Non‑Emergency Line:** 404‑656‑4000 (or 911 if it’s an emergency). |
| 3 | **Use the 311 service** for non‑urgent complaints, including noise. | **311 Phone:** 404‑656‑3111 (or dial 311 on your cell phone if you’re in Atlanta). |
| 4 | **Submit online** via the City of Atlanta’s official website. | **Website:** [Atlanta.gov/311](https://www.atlanta.gov/311) – choose “Noise” or “Public Safety” as the category. |
| 5 | **Check the Atlanta Noise Ordinance** for details on permissible noise levels and times. | **Ordinance:** [Noise Ordinance PDF](https://www.atlanta.gov/311/noise-ordinance) (or search “Atlanta noise ordinance” on the city’s website). |

### Quick Reference

- **Atlanta Police Department (APD) – Non‑Emergency Line:** 404‑656‑4000  
- **Atlanta 311 Service:** 404‑656‑3111 (or dial 311)  
- **Online 311 Portal:** https://www.atlanta.gov/311  
- **Noise Ordinance:** Search “Atlanta noise ordinance” on the city’s website or view the PDF linked above.

### Why the City Council Isn’t the Direct Contact

The city council sets policy and passes ordinances, but day‑to‑day enforcement of noise regulations is handled by the police department. If you have concerns about how a noise complaint is being handled, you can bring them to the attention of the council by contacting your city council member or attending a council meeting.

---

**Bottom line:** Yes, you can report noise complaints in Atlanta, but you’ll do so through the city’s police department or 311 service, not directly to the city council.
